messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test expects:
  - OptionBuilder.withDescription("JUnit").create('"') should throw IllegalArgumentException because '"' is an illegal option character.
  - Regardless of that failure, the builder must be reset so that a subsequent OptionBuilder.create('x').getDescription() returns null.

- How the code behaves:
  - OptionBuilder.withDescription(String) sets a static field:
    - at 298–302: OptionBuilder.description = newDescription; return instance;
  - OptionBuilder.create(char) delegates to create(String):
    - at 314–317: return create(String.valueOf(opt));
  - OptionBuilder.create(String) builds the Option and only then resets:
    - at 349: Option option = new Option(opt, description);
    - at 352–358: sets properties on the created option
    - at 360: OptionBuilder.reset();
  - Option(String, String) delegates to the full constructor:
    - at 88–91: this(opt, null, false, description);
  - Option(String, String, boolean, String) validates the opt:
    - at 119–125: OptionValidator.validateOption(opt);
  - OptionValidator.validateOption(String) throws on illegal characters:
    - at 58–61: throw new IllegalArgumentException("illegal option value '" + ch + "'");

- Why the failure occurs:
  - When create('"') is called, OptionBuilder.create(String) attempts to instantiate Option at line 349.
  - Option’s constructor calls OptionValidator.validateOption, which throws IllegalArgumentException for '"'.
  - Because the exception is thrown before OptionBuilder.reset() (line 360) executes, the builder’s static state (e.g., description = "JUnit") is not cleared.
  - The subsequent call OptionBuilder.create('x') reuses the stale description, so getDescription() returns "JUnit" instead of null, causing the test to fail.

- Root cause:
  - OptionBuilder.create(String) resets the builder only after successful option creation. It does not reset in a finally block, so on exception paths the state remains dirty.
  - This matches the bug report: “OptionBuilder is not reset in case of an IAE at create,” leading to unintended carry-over of settings.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
